messages.text: just opened the draft doc. abstract is due in 8 days but i want it done by friday so sofia can look at it.
also realized i forgot to mention: we still need the trigram ablation numbers for the experiments section. without that, the reviewer will ask why we keep that stage if embeddings handle it.
i was hoping you wouldn't bring that up tonight 😅 i can run it tomorrow morning. the pipeline is cached so it should be fast, but i need to clear the alias cache first or the results will be garbage.
yes, definitely clear the cache. do not trust any run where the model decision count is zero. that's how we ended up with the 'vacation photos' incident last week.
lol okay. i'll script a fresh run with --clear-cache and log the stage breakdown for all 2,946 strings. i'll have the table ready by noon.
perfect. i'm going to draft the related-work section now. it's going to be a mess because i keep finding papers from 2014 that do exactly what we do but with worse tech.
that's actually helpful for the novelty claim. if they used cloud apis and neo4j, we can emphasize the local-first + privacy angle in the intro. diego will love that.
agreed. i'll write method and eval sections. you take experiments and tables? want to make sure the numbers match exactly what's in the repo right now.
sounds good. i'll pull the latest commit hash and cite it in the footnotes so there's no ambiguity about which version of the code produced these numbers.
you're actually a good collaborator. okay, i'm off to write until my brain melts. ping me if the ablation run crashes or if you need help with the latex tables.
will do. good luck with the related work. i'm starting the cache clear now so it's running while i sleep.
